findings.summary: Page 1 ends its "Erasure Is Total" section with five unheaded code blocks lifted from chapters 6, 9 and 10, every one of which uses machinery that is not introduced until pages 4–6.
findings.evidence: Page 1, after the "Pass A Value Instead" callout: `class Stack<T>`, `function Ser<B extends Ctor<object>>(Base: B)`, `type Push<T extends unknown[], V> = [...T, V] // variadic tuples pair with infer`, `type Aw<T> = T extends { then(cb: (v: infer V) => any): any } ? Aw<V> : T`, and `type Equal<A, B> = (<T>() => T extends A ? 1 : 2) extends ...`. `Ctor` is only defined on page 4 (`type Ctor<T> = new (...a: any[]) => T`), conditional types on page 4 (`3. Conditional Types`), and `infer` on page 5 (`1. \`infer\` Captures A Slot` — "Declares a fresh variable inside `extends`").
findings.fix: Delete all five blocks from page 1. Move `Stack<T>` and the `Ser` mixin next to page 4's "4. Interfaces And Classes" / "6. Constructors And Mixins", `Push`/`Cat` and `Aw` into the infer section on pages 5–6, and `Equal` into page 6's distribution section beside the `[T]` bracket trick. Page 1 should end at the erasure callout and go straight into "1. Inference At The Call Site".

findings.summary: Section 6 is printed on page 1 while section 5, which declares the very types section 6 quizzes the reader on, does not appear until page 2.
findings.evidence: Page 1: heading "6. Order And Arity" with table rows "Pair<string> | needs 2 type args" and "bare `Box` | alias must be applied". Page 2 opens with heading "5. Declaring Parameters" and the code `class Box<T> { v!: T }` / `interface Pair<A, B> { a: A; b: B }`.
findings.fix: Swap the two: put "5. Declaring Parameters" (with the `Box`/`Pair`/`Result`/`<T,>` code and the "Scope And Naming" sidebox) before "6. Order And Arity", so `Pair<A, B>` and `Box<T>` are declared before the arity and bare-alias rules reference them.

findings.summary: The claim that conflicting inference candidates widen to a union is wrong — tsc reports an error instead.
findings.evidence: "pair(1, 'x')  // T = string | number" and the bullet "Inference widens to a union, it does not error."
findings.fix: Change the comment to "// Error: 'x' not assignable to number" and rewrite the bullet: tsc fixes T from the first candidate (number) and reports the second argument as an error; it does not union candidates. Union inference requires two parameters (`pair<A, B>`) or an explicit `pair<string | number>(1, 'x')`.

findings.summary: The caption promises a ten-page deck ending in a cheat sheet, but the deck is nine pages and stops mid-topic with no summary, trade-offs, or mistakes material.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages on the mechanics tsc actually runs ... Ends with a cheat sheet worth screenshotting." The deck has nine slides and the last block on page 9 is the bullet list "`NoInfer<T>` stops a slot producing candidates ... A variable passed in is already widened." Syllabus chapters "Comparisons and Trade-Offs", "Common Mistakes and Anti-Patterns" and "Summary: The Generics Cheat Sheet" appear nowhere in the content.
findings.fix: Add a tenth page carrying the cheat-sheet chapter (declare/constrain/default, the `<T, K extends keyof T>` shape, distribution and `[T]`, infer sites, mapped modifiers, variance, the decision rule), or amend the caption to the real page count and real ending.

findings.summary: The return type annotated for an indexed read is wrong under default compiler settings.
findings.evidence: "function first<T>(a: readonly T[]) {", "  return a[0]  // T | undefined"
findings.fix: Change the comment to "// T (add | undefined with noUncheckedIndexedAccess)", or write `return a.at(0)` / `a[0] as T | undefined`; by default `a[0]` is inferred as `T`, which is exactly the unsoundness the page-3 noUncheckedIndexedAccess tip is selling.

findings.summary: `keyof` and indexed access `T[K]` are used in worked signatures on pages 1 and 2 but are not defined until page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 1 callout "Read It Aloud": "pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(items: T[], key: K): T[K][]". Page 2: table row "K extends keyof U | one key of U" and `declare function get<T, K extends keyof T>(o: T, k: K): T[K]`. Page 3 is the first definition: "1. `keyof` Basics — Union of the type's public property keys."
findings.fix: Add a one-line gloss at the first use on page 1 ("`keyof T` = the union of T's keys; `T[K]` = the type at key K — full treatment on page 3"), or move the "1. `keyof` Basics" table and bullets ahead of the constraints section so the bound `K extends keyof T` lands after the operator it uses.

findings.summary: Constraints are said to be restricted to earlier type parameters, but TypeScript has allowed a constraint to reference a later type parameter since 1.8.
findings.evidence: "Constraints see earlier params only, left to right." / "`<K extends keyof T, T>` is illegal, order matters."
findings.fix: Drop both bullets or invert them: `<K extends keyof T, T>` compiles fine (type parameters may constrain each other in any order, e.g. `assign<T extends U, U>`); only circular constraints are rejected. The left-to-right rule applies to *defaults* only — which the same page already states correctly under section on defaults.

findings.summary: An unheaded bullet list on default type parameters is stranded at the end of page 3, two sections before its own heading "1. Default Type Parameters" on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 3 final block (no heading): "Defaults make trailing parameters optional." / "May reference earlier params: `<T, U = T[]>`." / "`<T extends string = number>` errors: default must fit bound." Page 4 then runs "4. Interfaces And Classes", "5. Structural Traps", "6. Constructors And Mixins" before reaching "1. Default Type Parameters" with `interface Options<T = string> { value: T }`.
findings.fix: Move that bullet list to page 4, immediately after the "1. Default Type Parameters" code block, so the `T = string` syntax is shown before the rules about defaults are stated.

findings.summary: `KeysOfType` on page 3 is built from mapped-type and conditional-type syntax, neither of which is taught until pages 4 and 6–7.
findings.evidence: Page 3, "3. Key-Driven Patterns": `type KeysOfType<T, V> = { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] extends V?K:never }[keyof T]`. Conditional types begin on page 4 ("3. Conditional Types"); mapped-type iteration and the `-?` modifier are first explained on pages 6–7 ("Iterate a key union, emit a new object type. / Modifiers add or strip `?` and `readonly`").
findings.fix: Move `KeysOfType` and its `FnKeys` bullets to page 7, next to the `NoFns<T>` key-remapping example, and keep page 3's key-driven section to the `set<T, K extends keyof T>` pattern only.

findings.summary: The recursive template-literal route parser is shown as the second conditional-type example, before the reader is told what a conditional type is and one page before `infer` is introduced.
findings.evidence: Page 4: heading "3. Conditional Types" → `type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false` → immediately `type Params<S> = S extends \`${string}:${infer P}/${infer R}\` ? P | Params<R> : ... // route parser sketch`. The explanation "A compile-time ternary judged by assignability. / Not by any runtime value" is the first block of page 5, and "1. `infer` Captures A Slot" comes later on page 5.
findings.fix: Move the explanatory bullets and the "Deferred Bites Implementations" callout up so they follow `IsString` directly, and relocate the `Params` route-parser sketch to after the infer section (page 6, next to "3. Match Shapes").

findings.summary: The bullet "That asymmetry ..." has no antecedent: the asymmetry it refers to is only stated in a table on the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 5 last block: "That asymmetry is variance leaking into inference. / Contravariant sites intersect the candidates." Page 6 first block: heading "2. Position Decides The Join" with table rows "covariant slots | a union" and "parameter slots | an intersection".
findings.fix: Move the "2. Position Decides The Join" heading and its table ahead of this bullet list, so the covariant-unions / contravariant-intersects rule is stated before it is called "that asymmetry".

findings.summary: "covariant" and "contravariant" are used as load-bearing terms in the infer section a full page before variance is defined.
findings.evidence: Page 6 table "Same name in | Combines to" with rows "covariant slots" and "parameter slots"; page 5 bullet "Contravariant sites intersect the candidates." Variance is first defined on page 7: "3. The Variance Question — Given Dog extends Animal, when is F<Dog> assignable to F<Animal>?"
findings.fix: Either gloss the terms inline in the infer table ("covariant = output slots, e.g. return types" / "contravariant = parameter slots") with a forward pointer to the variance section, or relabel the rows as "return-type slots" / "parameter slots" and save the variance vocabulary for page 7.

findings.summary: The variance table lists Array<T> as the example of an invariant type, contradicting TypeScript's actual (unsoundly covariant) arrays and the rest of the same page.
findings.evidence: Table row "invariant | neither | Array<T>, Map<K,V>" against the same page's "const animals: Animal[] = dogs  // allowed", "// arrays are unsoundly covariant, by design" and the later row "T[] | covariant, unsafe".
findings.fix: Replace the invariant example with a type TypeScript really measures as invariant — e.g. `interface Store<in out T>` from the next section, or a `{ get(): T; set(x: T): void }` written with function-typed (not method) members — and leave `Array<T>` only in the covariant rows.

findings.summary: The caption advertises ten pages but the set contains nine.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages on the mechanics tsc actually runs" — slides array holds 9 entries (Why Generics Exist … Inference Priority And NoInfer).
findings.fix: Change "Ten pages" to "Nine pages", or add the missing tenth page.

findings.summary: The table implies the built-in Promise has a `void` default type argument, which it does not.
findings.evidence: Table row "Promise<T = void> | 90% omit the arg"
findings.fix: Drop the row or rewrite it as a declaration-side example that isn't a lib type (e.g. "`emit<T = void>()` | callers omit the arg"); `Promise` has no default and bare `Promise` fails with "Generic type 'Promise<T>' requires 1 type argument(s)".

findings.summary: The structural-typing example uses a property name that does not match the Box class declared earlier in the set.
findings.evidence: "`Box<string>` and `{ value: string }` interchange freely." against page 2's "class Box<T> { v!: T }"
findings.fix: Make the shapes agree — either say "`Box<string>` and `{ v: string }` interchange freely" or redeclare Box as `class Box<T> { value!: T }`.

findings.summary: ElementOf is presented as a standard-library utility type, but TypeScript ships no such type.
findings.evidence: Sidebox titled "Stdlib Built On infer" listing "ElementOf for array element types."
findings.fix: Remove the ElementOf line (or mark it as the hand-written `type ElementOf<T> = T extends (infer E)[] ? E : never` shown two blocks earlier) and replace it with a real lib type such as ConstructorParameters or NoInfer.

findings.summary: The result of `ToArray` is quoted in bullets before the block that defines `ToArray`.
findings.evidence: Page 6, "4. Distribution Rule" bullets: "`ToArray<string|number>` is `string[] | number[]`." The definition `type ToArray<T> = T extends any ? T[] : never` is in the following code block.
findings.fix: Put the code block with `ToArray` and `Off` immediately after the "4. Distribution Rule" heading, then the bullets that report its results.

findings.summary: The section heading "3. Higher-Order Inference" is left orphaned at the bottom of the right column with no body text under it, and its bullets appear on page 9.
findings.evidence: Page 8, right column, last element: "3. Higher-Order Inference" followed by empty page area to the bottom margin; the matching body ("TS 3.4: composing generics propagates free parameters.", "compose(f, g) can stay generic...") opens page 9 with no heading.
findings.fix: Keep the heading with its first bullets: push "3. Higher-Order Inference" to the top of page 9's flow (heading keep-with-next rule) so it is not emitted when its body cannot follow on the same page.
